vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: gws-tasks
Version: 1.0.1

The skill bundle provides a standard interface for managing Google Tasks via a CLI tool named 'gws'. The SKILL.md file contains legitimate documentation for task and tasklist management operations (CRUD), and there are no signs of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's commands match its stated purpose (it wraps a gws CLI for Google Tasks), but the runtime instructions reference an external shared SKILL.md for auth and potentially-create files without declaring what credentials or config it needs, which is an inconsistency worth verifying before install.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Google Tasks) match the required binary 'gws' and the SKILL.md which documents gws tasks commands and resources. The requested binary is appropriate for the described functionality.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions tell the agent to read ../gws-shared/SKILL.md for auth, global flags, and security rules and to run 'gws generate-skills' if missing. That references files outside this skill and instructs potential file creation/modification; the skill does not document what exactly will be read or written.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files are provided (instruction-only), so nothing will be downloaded or written by the skill itself. Risk depends on the installed 'gws' binary which is external to the skill.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md implies authentication is required (it points to a shared auth SKILL.md), yet the registry metadata lists no required environment variables or primary credential. This mismatch leaves unclear what secrets (OAuth tokens, API keys, etc.) the agent must have and where they are read from.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and there is no indication the skill requests persistent elevated placement or modifies other skills. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default (not a concern on its own).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a thin wrapper around a local 'gws' CLI for Google Tasks and is mostly coherent — but before installing, confirm: (1) that you trust and have installed the 'gws' binary from a reputable source; (2) where authentication is stored and what credentials (OAuth tokens, API keys, env vars, or files) the shared '../gws-shared/SKILL.md' expects; and (3) what 'gws generate-skills' would create on disk. If you cannot inspect the referenced gws-shared SKILL.md or prefer not to allow the CLI to generate files, treat this as untrusted and run it only in a sandbox. If you want a firmer assessment, provide the contents of the referenced ../gws-shared/SKILL.md or detail how your environment provides gws auth (env vars vs interactive OAuth).
